newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italian sales boost European car market.
newsitem.headline: Italian sales boost European car market.

text.p: Car sales in Western Europe soared 9 percent year-on-year in June, partly reflecting a booming Italian market triggered by an incentive programme, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association said Tuesday.
"This 9 percent is due to some special effects ... and some countries are recovering," said Jorg Schroder, the association's director of trade and economics.
In the first six months of the year, new car registrations rose a more modest 1.7 percent to 6,991,700.
The increase in new registrations to 1,135,600 cars in June from 1,042,000 the same month last year came after a year-on-year decline of 1.9 percent in May.

In June, Italy stood out with a 50.7 percent jump in registrations to 222,800 cars following a year-on-year increase of 43.2 percent in May -- thanks to a national cash incentive programme that encourages motorists to turn in old cars for scrap in exchange for buying new models.
The programme was introduced in January.
In contrast, the French market declined 30.7 percent to 93,200 units, still depressed by the end of a similar incentive programme in France more than six months ago.
Other national markets showed wide variations.
The Danish market declined 39.5 percent to 7,800 units while the Austrian market rose by 31 percent to 26,600 and the Swedish market by 22.9 percent to 20,900 units.
Germany, the largest car market in Europe, recovered by 8.4 percent to 343,000 after a decline of 12.9 percent in May.
Among car makers, Fiat sales jumped 25.1 percent to 146,000, making it the second largest company in Europe after Germany's Volkswagen, whose sales rose 10.8 percent to 213,200 units.
As a result, Fiat's market share rose to 12.9 percent from 11.2 percent in June last year, still far behind Volkswagen's 18.8 percent share.
Japanese and Korean car makers also strengthened their positions, increasing sales by 15.3 percent and 23.8 percent respectively.
U.S. giant General Motors Corp. lost market share, to 12.3 percent from 13.0 percent, despite a rise in sales of 3.5 percent from last year.
Ford Motor Co., however, increased its share to 11.9 percent from 11.5 percent as a result of a 12.9 percent increase in sales.
